t: Educated at Harrow and Cambridge, Nehru gave up the law for the nationalist movement, spent over nine years in British prisons and became, with Gandhi's backing, the leader who called for complete independence in 1929.

As India's first prime minister for nearly seventeen years he promoted parliamentary democracy, secularism, science and planned industrialisation, and led the Non-Aligned Movement between the Cold War blocs.
His reputation suffered from India's defeat in the 1962 war with China, and critics fault his economic protectionism, his handling of Kashmir and what they call his selective secularism.
dyk: Nehru's best-known books, among them The Discovery of India, Glimpses of World History and An Autobiography, were all written in jail; Letters from a Father to His Daughter was written to Indira, then ten years old.
ev: Jawaharlal Nehru is born in Allahabad, the son of the barrister Motilal Nehru
He is imprisoned for anti-government activity, the first of eight detentions up to 1945
As Congress president at Lahore he carries the resolution for complete independence
After the Quit India resolution he is arrested with the Congress working committee
He becomes the first prime minister of independent India and gives the "Tryst with Destiny" speech
He is a key organiser of the Bandung Conference of newly independent nations from Asia and Africa
Nehru dies in office and is succeeded by Lal Bahadur Shastri

f.born: 14 November 1889, in Allahabad in British India; first child of the barrister and Congress leader Motilal Nehru and Swarup Rani, of the Kashmiri Pandit community
f.died: 27 May 1964, in office, of what was believed to be a heart attack; cremated by Hindu rites at the Shantivan on the banks of the Yamuna
f.role: Barrister of the Allahabad High Court (from 1912); general secretary and several times president of the Indian National Congress (president from 1929); interim prime minister (1946-1947); first Prime Minister of India (1947-1964), holding External Affairs throughout
f.known: The Lahore resolution for complete independence (1929); the "Tryst with Destiny" speech; parliamentary democracy and secularism; planned industrialisation and a mixed economy; the Indian Institutes of Technology and other institutions; the Non-Aligned Movement; the Sino-Indian War of 1962; The Discovery of India and An Autobiography
